courses.title: Computer Programming
courses.description: A first course that treats the machine as visible rather than hidden. Students learn C not as a syntax exercise but as a way to see how memory, addresses, and control flow actually behave — the foundation everything in later semesters is built on.

units.label: Unit I
units.title: Fundamentals
units.topics: Problem solving, algorithms and flowcharts; the compilation model; identifiers, data types, storage classes; operators, precedence and type conversion; formatted input and output.

units.label: Unit II
units.title: Control flow
units.topics: Conditional statements and the dangling-else problem; switch; while, do-while and for loops; break, continue, goto; loop invariants and tracing.

units.label: Unit III
units.title: Functions and recursion
units.topics: Declaration, definition and prototypes; call by value; scope and lifetime; the call stack; recursion — factorial, Fibonacci, Towers of Hanoi; the preprocessor and macros.

units.label: Unit IV
units.title: Arrays and strings
units.topics: One- and two-dimensional arrays; passing arrays to functions; matrix operations; character arrays, the string.h library, and writing your own string routines.

units.label: Unit V
units.title: Pointers and memory
units.topics: Address arithmetic; pointers to arrays and functions; call by reference; dynamic allocation with malloc, calloc, realloc, free; common leaks and dangling-pointer bugs.

units.label: Unit VI
units.title: Structures and files
units.topics: Structures, nested structures, arrays of structures; unions, enums and bit-fields; typedef; text and binary file I/O; command-line arguments.

resources.item: Lecture slides, Units I–VI (PDF)
Pointer and memory-layout diagrams; dry-run worksheets
Lab sheets 1–12 with expected input/output for each program
Worked solutions released after each lab deadline
Debugging exercises — 30 programs with deliberate bugs to find

King, C Programming: A Modern Approach, 2nd edition, W. W. Norton.

courses.title: Data Structure
courses.description: Choosing the representation that makes an operation cheap. The course pairs every structure with the cost of its operations, and every lab with a measurement — so that asymptotic claims are something students verify rather than memorize.

units.label: Unit I
units.title: Analysis and arrays
units.topics: Abstract data types; asymptotic notation and cost models; time–space trade-offs; one- and multi-dimensional arrays, address calculation, sparse matrices.

units.label: Unit II
units.title: Linked lists
units.topics: Singly, doubly and circular lists; insertion, deletion and reversal; polynomial and long-integer arithmetic; comparison with array-backed lists.

units.label: Unit III
units.title: Stacks and queues
units.topics: Array and linked implementations; infix–postfix conversion and evaluation; recursion and the call stack; circular queues, deques, priority queues.

units.label: Unit IV
units.title: Trees
units.topics: Binary trees and traversals; binary search trees; AVL rotations and balance; B-trees and B+-trees; threaded trees; expression trees.

units.label: Unit V
units.title: Heaps and hashing
units.topics: Binary heaps, heapify, heapsort; hash functions; separate chaining and open addressing; load factor and rehashing.

units.label: Unit VI
units.title: Graphs
units.topics: Representations; BFS and DFS; topological sort; minimum spanning trees (Prim, Kruskal); shortest paths (Dijkstra, Bellman–Ford, Floyd–Warshall).

units.label: Unit VII
units.title: Sorting and searching
units.topics: Insertion, selection, bubble, merge, quick, radix and counting sorts; lower bounds for comparison sorting; linear and binary search; external sorting.

resources.item: Lecture slides, Units I–VII (PDF)
Complexity cheat-sheet and rotation/rebalancing worksheets
Lab sheets 1–12 in C: lists, stacks, BST, AVL, heap, graph traversals
Reference implementations and a timing harness for empirical complexity plots
Problem set with graded difficulty and previous-year papers

Tenenbaum, Langsam and Augenstein, Data Structures Using C, Pearson.

courses.title: Database Management Systems
courses.description: What it takes to keep shared data correct while many people change it at once. The course moves from modelling and the relational algebra behind SQL to the concurrency control and storage machinery that makes the guarantees hold.

units.label: Unit I
units.title: Database concepts and modelling
units.topics: File systems versus DBMS; three-schema architecture and data independence; ER and extended ER modelling; mapping ER designs to relations.

units.label: Unit II
units.title: Relational model and algebra
units.topics: Relations, keys and integrity constraints; selection, projection, join, division; tuple and domain relational calculus; expressive equivalence.

units.label: Unit III
units.title: SQL
units.topics: DDL and DML; joins, nested and correlated subqueries; aggregation and grouping; views; triggers and stored procedures; embedded and dynamic SQL.

units.label: Unit IV
units.title: Design theory
units.topics: Functional dependencies, closure and minimal cover; 1NF through BCNF; 4NF and multivalued dependencies; lossless-join and dependency-preserving decomposition.

units.label: Unit V
units.title: Transactions and concurrency
units.topics: ACID properties; schedules and serializability; two-phase locking, timestamp ordering and optimistic control; deadlock handling; logging and recovery.

units.label: Unit VI
units.title: Storage, indexing and beyond
units.topics: File organization; B+-tree and hash indexes; query processing and cost-based optimization; introduction to distributed and NoSQL systems.

resources.item: Lecture slides, Units I–VI (PDF)
Normalization worked examples and serializability test worksheets

courses.title: Digital Image Processing
courses.description: From how a sensor turns light into an array of numbers to how a convolutional network decides what those numbers mean. The course keeps a forensic thread running through it: every operation we study — resampling, JPEG quantization, filtering — leaves a trace, and those traces are what makes tampering detectable.

units.label: Unit I
units.title: Digital image fundamentals
units.topics: Image formation and the human visual system; sampling and quantization; spatial and intensity resolution; pixel relationships and distance measures; image file formats.

units.label: Unit II
units.title: Intensity transformations and histogram processing
units.topics: Log, power-law and piecewise-linear transforms; histogram equalization and specification; local enhancement; arithmetic and logical operations on images.

units.label: Unit III
units.title: Spatial filtering
units.topics: Correlation and convolution; smoothing and order-statistic filters; sharpening with the Laplacian and unsharp masking; gradient operators — Sobel, Prewitt, Roberts.

units.label: Unit IV
units.title: Frequency-domain processing
units.topics: 2-D DFT and its properties; the FFT; ideal, Butterworth and Gaussian low- and high-pass filters; homomorphic filtering; the DCT and why JPEG uses 8×8 blocks.

units.label: Unit V
units.title: Restoration and noise models
units.topics: Gaussian, impulse, Rayleigh and periodic noise; mean, order-statistic and adaptive filters; inverse and Wiener filtering; estimating the degradation function.

units.label: Unit VI
units.title: Compression
units.topics: Redundancy and fidelity criteria; Huffman and arithmetic coding; run-length and LZW; transform coding and the JPEG pipeline; a note on JPEG artefacts as forensic evidence.

units.label: Unit VII
units.title: Morphology and segmentation
units.topics: Erosion, dilation, opening, closing, hit-or-miss; boundary extraction and skeletons; thresholding including Otsu's method; region growing, splitting and merging; watershed segmentation.

units.label: Unit VIII
units.title: Colour, representation and learning
units.topics: RGB, HSI and CMYK models; pseudo-colour processing; boundary and regional descriptors; introduction to CNNs for image analysis and to image forensics as an application area.
